scope: Official compile-time option, build, VFS, I/O methods, extension and function API documentation

claims.claim: SQLITE_OMIT_* options are mostly unsupported and may not work reliably with a prebuilt amalgamation
claims.notes: The same option set may need to be passed to Lemon and mkkeywordhash when generating canonical-source builds.

claims.claim: Custom amalgamation generation should configure the canonical source tree and use the sqlite3.c make target
sqlite3_vfs defines the OS interface and includes xOpen, xDelete, xAccess and other platform services
sqlite3_io_methods defines per-file read, write, truncate, sync, lock, shared-memory and related operations
claims.locator: OS Interface File Virtual Methods Object

claims.claim: Extension loading is disabled by default; SQLITE_DBCONFIG_ENABLE_LOAD_EXTENSION can enable only the C API while keeping SQL load_extension disabled
SQLITE_DETERMINISTIC and SQLITE_INNOCUOUS express different function properties and must not be applied casually
sqlite3_create_function_v2 registers application-defined scalar, aggregate or window callbacks
The tracing VFS example intercepts xOpen and delegates to the parent VFS; it does not transform or encrypt file bytes
claims.notes: The code is independently authored and tested against the system SQLite library.

claims.claim: A complete VFS must preserve file, sync, lock and shared-memory contracts, not merely wrap main database xRead/xWrite
claims.notes: The article explicitly distinguishes a tracing wrapper from an encryption implementation.

claims.claim: The SQLite Encryption Extension is a separately licensed extension rather than a generic core encryption switch
SQLCipher is a third-party encrypted SQLite distribution
ECB mode reveals repeated plaintext block patterns and is not a suitable database-file encryption design
claims.notes: The tutorial does not publish a homemade production encryption protocol.
